paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, we're going to move on to health.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: To have good health means I need to have a lot of money.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's too difficult to change my body.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's too much work to eat healthy.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: This is the opposite, but: I can't afford to take care of my body.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm already healthy enough.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I love sugar way too much to give it up.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I need my morning coffee.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm inherently broken, and I'm always going to be sick.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: There's something wrong with me, and I don't know what it is, and no one can find the solution.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm just going to get old and die anyway, so — viva la vida, right?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: God — Ricky Martin. Viva la vida loca.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Anything else that comes up?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Sorry, we're going to go through all of them, because I think it's important. Work.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Work is a modern form of slavery.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I will never get my dream job.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Work has to be hard.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If I don't enjoy my job, I'm doing something right.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm never going to be happy at work.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All the good jobs are taken.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: The economy is bad.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's too late for me to do the thing that I truly love.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: My coworkers are out to get me.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Everyone else gets the good jobs, and I always get the crappy ones.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Here's a relevant one: my Lama doesn't give me the job that I really want.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Everyone else gets a job, but I don't.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Everyone's laughing. But if you're laughing, you're kind of like, yeah, this is me. Paola had a really great metaphor for this: this is already in your user manual, and you just think it's normal — that this is just how life is. "I am this." And that's writing your whole script.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, last section. Self-worth. After the others, this one's going to be the hardest.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I will never be happy until I have the things I want.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: People won't pay attention to me or love me if I have no money.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I know a lot of men who are afraid to be in a relationship because they don't believe they have a good enough job. Or they get into a relationship and then feel like they have to save everything — "save" as take care of everything.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Happiness means I have to give up on the physical world entirely.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm not worthy of attention.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I have nothing to give other people.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm perfect, and I don't need to change.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That one — you thought we were going to go in the other direction. Think about that one. "I don't need to change, because I'm like that, because I'm good."

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I will always be imperfect.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I was just born in the wrong generation.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Nobody will ever understand me.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm always going to fail.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Successful people are only successful because they deceived others.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's someone else's fault that I'm not successful.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If that one thing hadn't happened, I'd be wealthy now. If I had just bought the damn Bitcoin in 2010, then everything would be totally fine.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I can't ever get out of debt.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I don't have time to do this kind of thing we're doing in class right now. I can't work on myself.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: To be successful means I need to be the best at everything.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm too stupid to be successful.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: What other things do you say to yourself? In your own language, your own words.

chapters.title: Choose one, and shine a light on it

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now you can see how this would turn into a ten-week workshop. But this is just a start. So what I'd like you to do — we just did five categories. Money. Relationships. Health. Work. And self-worth. Which one had the strongest reaction in you? Some of them might be like, yeah, it's not so bad. For me — yeah, I have some limiting beliefs about money, but it's not what really keeps me up at night. I've got a great V Houses team that's building a fundraising machine. Like Katya.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And Katya suggested that we should fundraise using seeds. Duh. I don't worry about it that much. I'm comfortable. But relationships? That brings up a lot more stuff for me. It doesn't mean I don't have things to work on on the money side — I still buy lottery tickets, with the hope that someday I won't have to worry about anything. Which is totally ridiculous to think that way. Everyone who's wealthy dies. There's no amount of money that's going to stop you from dying.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So which one of those five were you like — yeah, that's my thing? And then, within that category, choose one. Not ten, not two. One. And have the discipline to put that into your awareness. Shine a light on it, and just simply notice, over the next week or so. I guarantee something will happen where you'll hear that in your head — you're going to hear those words in your head. And then watch how that changes when you do that. Watch what you choose to do afterwards, because the seed you're planting afterwards is going to be recreating this. Once you shine the light on it, you're going to have a moment to be like — maybe I could do something a little different right now. And so you're actually stopping it via absence. It's an absence of that old seed, and you're putting the new one in place. Just keep it up for a while, and notice what might change.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But please, for the love of seeds, don't try to do all of them at once. Because you won't be able to — you won't be able to change any of them. Choose the one that's the weakest for you. You don't need a whole mountain of self-discipline to do it. You just need a spoonful of self-discipline. Just to notice. And if you're not able to choose one, just choose the one that comes up the next time you get upset. Next time you get upset, be like — ah, that person didn't do what I said. Really? Why do you have people around you who don't do what you say? "Because I'm someone that people don't listen to." Oh, are you really? Is that a belief you have — that people won't listen to you? "Well, yeah, no one listens to me." Why? What am I doing right after I realize people don't listen to me? Guaranteed, I'm planting the seeds for them not to listen to me. 100% guaranteed.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then — four steps and four powers. The end. And I say that lovingly. It's simple, but it's also challenging, because that's how this goes. You have to look at yourself. But the point is that when you notice, go to the positive immediately. Don't engage the story. If you want to engage the story, go to the therapist — get it all out, understand it. I'm not dissing therapy; it's amazing, because you might need to talk it out, because you may not know why, and that's part of the process. But then, for the love of seeds, put a different story in. Like I put a different story in with Juan the other day. I'm going to commit to listening to people for their entire sentence, and not half the sentence, before I react. Because that's planting a different seed. And eventually it'll change.
